bucket: circle entries report more administrative and governance dysfunction plus operational failures in support services (turnover, secrecy, favoritism, misallocation, cover‑ups, counselor/scheduling/records breakdowns) than square entries
definition: This bucket groups reviewer claims about leadership and district failures—frequent principal/superintendent turnover, secretive or arbitrary firings, nepotism/favoritism, deliberate image‑management or suppressed complaints—and related operational breakdowns such as lost transcripts, scheduling errors, inaccessible counselors, 50% grading policies, and intentional credit manipulation (e.g., 'They keep everything a secret... fired a great teacher,' 'Counselors are never available,' 'lost testing scores,' 'some teachers are purposely failing the students meaning more money for the school'). These are governance and service-delivery problems distinct from classroom instruction and are reported more often in Circle.

bucket: circle entries report more chronic facilities, resource, and operational shortfalls (overcrowding, HVAC/pests, missing materials, mandatory fees and opaque charges) than square entries
definition: Encompasses concrete, recurring operational deficits: overcrowded cafeterias/classrooms, broken HVAC for years, pest infestations, missing textbooks/equipment, required costly fees and opaque charging practices (e.g., pay for temporary IDs), and poorly maintained buildings—circle reviewers repeatedly cite no A/C, rats, peeling paint, and opaque student fees whereas square reviewers seldom raise those exact resource failures.

bucket: circle entries report more concrete operational and facility shortcomings (outdated curriculum/technology gaps, missing textbooks, overcrowding, cleanliness/food safety problems, parking/traffic hazards, and mixed renovation/funding narratives) than square entries
definition: This bucket covers reviews documenting tangible infrastructure or instructional‑resource problems—no/old textbooks, 'Stone Age' curriculum, lack of AC, cockroaches, overcrowded classrooms, food safety, unmanaged student parking and traffic risks—often paired with mentions of renovation plans or funding shortfalls and staff paying out‑of‑pocket (examples: “lacks textbooks and reliable resources,” “the building is overcrowded…in desperate need of AC,” “cockroaches and worms,” and “undergoing renovation but lacks funding”). Include reviews that focus on physical or resourcing constraints, aging facilities, or technology/curriculum obsolescence rather than interpersonal or policy problems.

bucket: circle entries emphasize a smaller, close‑knit, family‑like community, higher personalized attention, and active alumni/parent involvement more than square entries
definition: This bucket collects circle reports of small class sizes, tight student–teacher relationships, multi‑year continuity programs (e.g., 6‑year arts), robust alumni ties, high parental volunteerism and individualized supports (lower student–teacher ratios, scheduled tutoring), contrasted with square's portrayal of a larger, more impersonal campus; examples include circle statements like 'class size about 15', 'you feel like family', many alumni returning to teach, and 'parent engagement above any school you've ever worked with.'

bucket: circle entries report pervasive safety, bullying, harassment, substance‑use, and discriminatory/toxic student‑climate problems with administrative inaction more than square entries
definition: These reviews describe frequent peer violence, daily bullying, sexual exploitation, drug incidents, weapons, staff‑perpetrated harassment and claims that administrators do nothing (e.g., “bullying is unbelievable…the administration does nothing,” “girls selling their bodies…drugs…staff incapable,” reports of drug busts and weapons). This bucket captures pieces that portray school safety and student‑climate breakdowns plus explicit failures to address them.

bucket: square entries display a more polarized instructional experience than circle entries: distinct pockets of high‑intensity individualized support and advanced teaching alongside uneven classroom quality and neglect of average/struggling students
definition: Many square reviews describe teachers who provide one‑on‑one help, extensive tutoring, counselors and AVID/one‑on‑one interventions AND, in the same school, report grade inflation for minimal effort, regular classroom disruption, inconsistent grading, or poor support for middle‑of‑the‑road learners and special‑education gaps (e.g., strong AP/IB instruction vs. ‘regular’ classes that are unchallenging or poorly differentiated); circle reviews lack this pronounced polarization.

bucket: square entries document more systemic administrative and governance failures — corruption/favoritism, hiring problems, grade manipulation, fiscal misprioritization, consolidation/board mismanagement, and routine communication/accountability breakdowns — than circle entries
definition: These reviews allege district‑ or school‑level misconduct and mismanagement (nepotistic hiring, favoritism to wealthy/athlete students, alleged grade bumps tied to evaluations), misallocated budgets, and persistent unresponsiveness or miscoordination from counselors and offices, while circle reviews do not present comparable evidence of systemic governance failure; examples include “The entire system…is corrupt,” “grades had been drastically bumped up in order for the teachers to look better,” and “Parents concerns are not well received and often dismissed.”

bucket: square entries emphasize broader extracurricular/arts/athletics breadth and stronger community/booster support but also more athletic prioritization and favoritism than circle entries
definition: This groups reviews that cite very large clubs/arts/music/theater offerings, unique programs (Cirque, aviation, state arts centers), strong booster/levy fundraising and families moving for the school, while also reporting athletics-dominant budgets, coach favoritism, and athletes getting preferential treatment (e.g., extensive music scholarships and top bands vs. claims that 'all they care about is athletics'), a pattern that contrasts with Circle.

bucket: square entries report more acute facility, operational and resourcing constraints (overcrowding, infrastructure problems, scheduling, technology and material shortages, sanitation and cafeteria concerns) than circle entries
definition: Square reviews contain concrete operational complaints—extreme enrollment/overcrowding figures, large class sizes, lost transcripts, asbestos/textbook shortages, inadequate testing computers, bad HVAC/food/parking, and budget-driven program cuts—whereas Circle reviews rarely detail this constellation of campus-level infrastructure and logistic failures.

bucket: square entries report more pervasive student-safety, bullying, harassment, substance‑use and racial/sexual‑orientation hostility — often paired with ineffective administrative responses — than circle entries
definition: Square reviews frequently recount fights, weapons/drug searches, sexual assault allegations, systemic bullying, racial harassment and LGBTQ/transphobic climates and describe administration failing to investigate or even blaming victims (examples: daily fights with police present, race wars, slurs left in bleachers, administration ‘did nothing’ or turned off a mic during a speech). Circle reviews, by contrast, more often describe a safer, inclusive environment and staff who intervene or support students.
